_comment: Copy to config.json and edit. config.json is gitignored: it holds credential hashes.
_bind: Loopback by default. Basic auth sends the credential on every note, reversibly encoded, so exposing this port directly to the internet would put member credentials in cleartext on the wire. Put TLS in front (a reverse proxy is enough) and pass --behind-tls-proxy; the server refuses to bind a non-loopback address without it.
_rateLimit: Two buckets. notesPerHour/burst is per credential and is a backstop against runaway cost, not a throttle on people — every note costs three model calls downstream, so a hook stuck in a loop or one leaked token can spend a month's budget before anyone looks. authAttemptsPerHour/authBurst is per address and sits BEFORE authentication, because verifying a credential runs scrypt on purpose: without it, an unauthenticated flood buys one deliberately-expensive hash per request and the timing-safety measure becomes a way to exhaust the CPU. Both are generous: a member having a heavy day must never be the reason a trap goes unrecorded.
_projects: One server, many projects. The key is the project id, which each repo states in its own .claude/settings.json as AGENT_KNOWLEDGE_PROJECT — that value is not a secret and is committed with the repo. Notes for different projects never share an inbox.

catalog-svc._members: The allow-list and the credential store are the same map on purpose. A separate list of permitted emails would be a second thing to keep in step, and the failure mode of it drifting is a departed member who can still write. Removing someone is deleting their entry. Generate one with: node aggregator/make-credential.js <email>

minh@example.com.hash: REPLACE — a member on two projects gets a separate credential for each, so revoking one does not touch the other
